editorial.headline: Residential Care, Under Government Stewardship
editorial.standfirst: This government-run residential care activity is nationally open to PMA ownership, while Bali does not block it under its risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity covers government-provided residential care that brings assisted living, medical treatment, nursing care and rehabilitation into one facility. Its defining feature is a permanent core team of registered or licensed practising nurses, supported by other staff, combining nursing with personal care. Typical services include administering medication, making medical diagnoses and treating wounds; these are usually delivered without the supervision of a physician assigned to the facility.

The scope is deliberately institutional rather than occasional. Care is provided within a residential setting and is organised around an enduring clinical and care workforce. The record identifies government as the provider of this activity. It does not list eligible business scales, so no scale-specific registration conclusion should be inferred beyond that stated governmental character.

The national PMA position remains open, permitting foreign ownership up to the 100% ceiling. That is the full national position contained in the record: foreign ownership may reach the stated maximum, under the cited investment basis. It does not alter the activity’s defined character as government-provided residential care; it simply describes the national PMA treatment recorded for it.

Bali requires a more exact reading of risk rather than a blanket assumption. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities, island-wide. This activity is recorded in Bali as medium-high/high risk and is not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with one recorded practical qualification: the position should be verified for the specific address. The honest conclusion is that Bali does not treat this activity as moratorium-blocked for PMA registration, while location-level verification remains part of the record’s instruction.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, the activity is not blocked by the moratorium, though the address still requires verification.
